content: Technical meetings will be organized by the WHO headquarters and regional offices as needed. The Verification Expert Panel (VEP) will provide recommendations to the Regional Director on whether the target of reducing hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection prevalence to less than 1% among children older than five years has been achieved. The Immunization and Vaccine Unit of the WHO regional office will act as the secretariat for the VEP. Conflict of Interest and Confidentiality When the VEP is formed and at the beginning of each meeting, members are required to complete a WHO declaration of interest form and sign a confidentiality agreement. All members must be experts in fields relevant to hepatitis B control, serving in their personal capacity, and must not represent the interests of any specific group or stakeholder. Members are prohibited from promoting the policies, views, or products of the organizations or institutions they are affiliated with. All background documents, papers, presentations, and reports presented to the VEP are to be treated as confidential and cannot be publicly disclosed or used by members without prior approval. As a WHO advisory body, neither the VEP as a whole nor individual members may speak or act on behalf of WHO or attend meetings on behalf of WHO without prior consent from the regional office or headquarters. Members are also prohibited from sharing information or making presentations on VEP-related topics without prior approval from WHO. VEP members will not receive remuneration for their participation; however, WHO will cover travel expenses related to VEP meetings in accordance with WHO policy. Operational Procedures The secretariat, VEP members, and the chairperson will maintain communication throughout the year. In-person VEP meetings will be conducted on an as-needed basis, with planning beginning at least three months in advance. Meetings may also be held via teleconference. Representatives from countries and external experts may be invited to attend meetings when appropriate. Agendas and relevant documents will be circulated in advance of each meeting. A summary report of the VEP meetings will be shared for comments and endorsement within two weeks of the meeting, and members are required to respond within two weeks of receiving the communication. When review teams complete the desk review of data for verifying the regional hepatitis B control goal through immunization, the VEP will discuss and approve the report submitted by the review team, either during a meeting or through email or other communication methods. For conflict of interest reasons, VEP members will not participate in the review team for their own country. This target is also part of the Global Health Sector Strategy on Viral Hepatitis (2016–2021), endorsed by the World Health Assembly, as a proxy for the 30% reduction in incidence aimed for in the strategy. It is also included in the Regional Action Plan for Viral Hepatitis (2016–2021), endorsed by the Regional Committee. The verification process involves a desk review of country data by an independent panel of experts who will advise WHO on whether the target has been achieved. Documenting the achievement of verification is critical to gaining further commitment to strengthening public health programs. The verification process includes the following steps: 1. The Ministry of Health submits a data and information package to WHO, including a request to initiate the process. 2. WHO convenes a verification team composed of three independent experts who are members of the verification panel. 3. The verification team reviews the data and information package, liaises with the Ministry of Health if additional information is needed, and informs WHO of its recommendation. Further instructions are provided for your reference. If you have any questions, the designated focal point or contact person is available to assist.
